candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — client rights, legal scope, continuity and care coordination
candidate.educational_objective: Prioritize sudden focal neurologic deficits as a time-sensitive emergency requiring immediate assessment and activation of the appropriate stroke response.

options.A: A client awaiting routine discharge teaching who has no new clinical concerns.
options.B: A client requesting a prescribed PRN sleep medication at the usual bedtime.
options.C: A client with sudden new facial droop, unilateral arm weakness, and difficulty speaking that began 20 minutes ago.
options.D: A client with chronic knee pain rated 7/10 whose assessment findings are otherwise unchanged.

candidate.rationale: CDC identifies sudden facial droop or unilateral weakness and sudden trouble speaking as stroke warning signs and emphasizes that every minute counts; emergency action is required. Among the four reports, C represents a new, time-sensitive neurologic emergency, whereas the other needs are routine or stable. Therefore C requires first assessment.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Sudden unilateral facial/arm weakness and difficulty speaking are stroke warning signs requiring immediate emergency evaluation.
candidate.source_locator: Signs and Symptoms — sudden numbness/weakness of face, arm, or leg especially one side; sudden confusion/trouble speaking; 'Every minute counts' emergency-action guidance.
